bug_description.original: Detailed report: https://oss-fuzz.com/testcase?key=5683497160671232 Project: c-ares Fuzzer: libFuzzer_c-ares_ares_parse_reply_fuzzer Fuzz target binary: ares_parse_reply_fuzzer Job Type: libfuzzer_asan_c-ares Platform Id: linux Crash Type: Stack-buffer-overflow WRITE 4 Crash Address: 0x7fbce74e3914 Crash State: ares_parse_aaaa_reply ares-test-fuzz.c Sanitizer: address (ASAN) Recommended Security Severity: High
bug_description.normalized: In c-ares ares_parse_a_reply, the function iterates all parsed DNS address nodes and writes TTL and IP data to the caller-provided addrttls buffer without checking that the loop index i is within the buffer's capacity (*naddrttls). When a crafted DNS response contains more A-record RRs than the caller's buffer capacity (5 elements in the fuzzer harness), the writes to addrttls[i] for i >= 5 overflow the stack-allocated buffer. ASAN detects a 4-byte stack-buffer-overflow write to addrttls[5].ttl.

source.description: Reads the attacker-controlled answer RR count from the DNS response header. This determines how many answer resource records the parser will process, controlling the number of address nodes created and ultimately the overflow extent in ares_parse_a_reply.
source.value_from: The DNS response buffer (abuf) is the raw fuzzer input passed through ares_parse_a_reply. DNS_HEADER_ANCOUNT reads the 16-bit answer count from bytes 6-7 of the DNS header within the attacker-controlled buffer.

relation.description: Source identity relation for the vulnerability-relevant value.

sink.description: Writes addrttls[i].ttl when i >= 5, overflowing the caller's 5-element stack-allocated struct ares_addrttl array. ASAN detects a 4-byte stack-buffer-overflow write at stack frame offset 108, which is info[5].ttl (the struct's second field, past the info array boundary at offset 104).

root_cause.description: The guard if (naddrttls) checks only that the pointer is non-NULL, omitting the bounds check i < *naddrttls. This allows the loop body to write to addrttls[i] for i values that exceed the caller's buffer capacity. The fix adds && i < *naddrttls to the condition.

tainted_value_origin.description: The answer count is read from the DNS response header. It controls the number of answer RRs parsed and the number of address nodes created, which determines naddrs in ares_parse_a_reply and thus the overflow distance.

parser_admitted.description: ares__parse_into_addrinfo2 returns ARES_SUCCESS for the PoC, confirming the DNS response has a valid header (alen >= HFIXEDSZ), qdcount == 1, an expandable question name, and well-formed answer RRs. The code proceeds past the error check at line 68 into the vulnerable address-iteration path.

fine_trace.note: Reads the 16-bit answer RR count from bytes 6-7 of the DNS header in the attacker-controlled buffer abuf. This value controls the for-loop iteration count at line 92, determining how many answer RRs are parsed and how many address nodes are created.

Inside the for-loop (line 92) iterating ancount answer RRs, each RR with rr_class==C_IN, rr_type==T_A, rr_len==sizeof(struct in_addr), and rr_name matching the question hostname creates and appends a new ares_addrinfo_node to the nodes list. The PoC encodes at least 6 such matching A records. After the loop, nodes are assigned to ai->nodes at line 234.

Counts all parsed address nodes into naddrs by traversing the ai.nodes linked list. With the PoC input, naddrs >= 6, exceeding the caller's addrttls capacity of 5 (the fuzzer harness allocates struct ares_addrttl info[5] and passes *naddrttls == 5). naddrs is used as the loop bound at line 151: for (i = 0; i < naddrs; i++).

Inside the for-loop bounded by naddrs, this guard checks only that the naddrttls pointer is non-NULL before writing to addrttls[i]. The missing bounds check i < *naddrttls allows the write when i >= 5, exceeding the caller's 5-element buffer. The fix changes this to if (naddrttls && i < *naddrttls).

Writes addrttls[i].ttl (line 158 or 160) and memcpy's addrttls[i].ipaddr (line 162) when i == 5, overflowing the caller's stack-allocated info[5] array. The struct layout places ipaddr at offset 0 and ttl at offset 4 within each element; the code writes ttl first. ASAN catches the 4-byte write at stack frame offset 108 (info base at offset 64 + 5*8 + 4 = 108), which is info[5].ttl, 4 bytes past the array end at offset 104.

format.name: libFuzzer binary blob for ares_parse_reply_fuzzer
format.contract: Crafted DNS response blob that, when parsed by ares__parse_into_addrinfo2, produces at least 6 A-record nodes matching the question hostname. The 6th iteration of the addrttls write loop in ares_parse_a_reply writes addrttls[5].ttl past the caller's 5-element stack buffer, triggering a 4-byte stack-buffer-overflow write at stack frame offset 108.
